name: Admin Accounting Cuenta de Cobro Create + Preview
description: Superuser creates a cuenta de cobro from the Cuentas de cobro tab button or from an income row action (kind expected/liquid, never lost; incomes with an active cuenta are blocked and expose a Ver cuenta de cobro navigation instead). The modal unifies with the clients module (ClientAutocomplete prefills name/NIT/cedula/email into an editable snapshot; inline client creation without leaving the flow), requires selecting an income via searchable combobox — or creating the expected income inline via the stacked income form. The combobox asks for the whole eligible ledger once (no client param) and narrows it on the page through two chip groups above the search box, each option carrying its own count: Alcance (Del cliente, the default once a client is picked and literally only their rows / Todos, the way to reach the still-unassigned incomes and the ones filed under someone else) and Estado (Todos / Esperados / Líquidos). Because the filtering is client-side the counts are exact and switching a chip costs no request, so the dropdown stays open and the cursor stays in the search box; the chips narrow the set the concept search then runs over, and both reset to their defaults whenever the client changes. Under Todos the rows split into De {cliente} / De otros clientes (each naming its owner) / Sin cliente, with the unassigned ones selectable on purpose — issuing adopts the client onto them, announced under the field before the send. A combination with no rows names itself («Acme Soluciones no tiene ingresos esperados.») and offers «Ver todos (N)» instead of rendering a blank panel, and the list now also closes on click-outside or Esc. Each group still declares how many rows it holds back; pairing an income with a different client raises an inline warning that blocks the preview until it is resolved, suggests an editable per-client consecutivo PA-{CODE}-{NNN} (sent only when edited), and ends in a mandatory step-2 preview rendering the REAL email subject/body and attached PDF (same backend pipeline as the send, rolled back server-side) side by side in a full-height two-column review with a draggable divider, independent scroll per column and a fixed header/footer, collapsing into Correo/PDF tabs below 1024px (opening on the PDF under 640px), before Confirmar y enviar issues, emails and links the document to the income. Marking an expected-linked cuenta as paid opens the Liquidar modal prefilled (never a silent settlement); a fully-settled income auto-marks its cuenta paid backend-side. Since Aug 2026 the Plazo de pago field accepts 0 — pago inmediato contra presentación — and a hint under it says what that does, shown only while the days mode is active since a 0 means nothing beside a fecha fija. A zero term issues the cuenta with no due date, so neither the PDF nor the client email prints a vencimiento line at all (the label goes with it, and the dates block closes ranks rather than leaving a gap). Negative terms are refused by the input's min and by the serializer, and an emptied field still falls back to the 8-day default (typed out-of-range values are clamped into 0–120 before the payload). Since Aug 2026 the step-2 PDF pane probes the served URL before mounting the viewer: a spinner while it resolves, the embed once it answers (the PDF endpoints ship X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN so the browser will render them framed at all), and on failure a panel in the app's own words pointing at Descargar / Abrir PDF — which keep working, so the review happens there and Confirmar y enviar stays available. Picking a hosting income that records the period it covers pre-fills the 'Período facturado' range instead of asking for it again. Since F7 (Aug 2026) a cuenta raised from a project-linked income lands in the list already showing that project: the draft inherits the income's project (kept in sync when the income's project changes later) and the Proyecto column reads the live FK.
